name: Chlorogenic acid
short: Injected into muscle (a different route) in 26 people with brain tumours: injection-site reactions, some severe (hardening). Intake: 5 blood-pressure trials (364 people) reported no adverse events.
text: In a 2015 meta-analysis of randomized trials of chlorogenic acid intake and blood pressure (the abstract does not state the route or products), five trials with 364 participants were pooled, and all included studies reported no adverse events; the authors note the trials were few, confined to Asian populations and funded by chlorogenic acid manufacturers. In a 6-month randomized, placebo-controlled trial in people with type 2 diabetes and fatty liver disease, chlorogenic acid alone did not differ from placebo on liver, metabolic or inflammatory measures, while blood insulin was higher than with placebo in the group taking chlorogenic acid together with caffeine; the abstract does not report adverse events. In a first-in-human phase I study in 26 people with recurrent high-grade glioma (a brain tumour), chlorogenic acid given by injection into muscle, a different route from supplements, was reported as well tolerated; the most common treatment-related adverse events were at the injection sites, and the only grade 3 or 4 (severe) events were hardening (induration) at the injection sites. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
